To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and characterised a novel human Pde4b cAMP phosphodiesterase isoform (HSPDE4B) that differs from the previously identified Pde4b splice variants, HSPDEB1 and Hspde4b2, by virtue of its 79 residue N terminus and that this isoform is expressed in both particulate and cytosol fractions in COS7 cells.
we have cloned and characterised a novel human PDES, HSPDE 4B3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the various isoforms of cAMP specific PDEs, and the factors that regulate their expression and function.
the molecular cloning of a novel human and rat PDC4B cAMP phosphodiesterase and the functional expression of these enzymes.
the molecular biology of cyclic AMP (cAMP) specific phosphodiesterases (PDE) and the cloning of the human cDNA of a novel PDE4B, HSPDEB4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is the first report of a novel human long form of a PDE, HSPDEB4, which has unique N terminal amino acids, compared to the two previously described human long form PDE4B isoform HSPDE4BI and HSPDEB42, and that the rat homologue, RNPDE4BI, is also a long form of PDE4B with unique amino acid sequence.
the three human PDE4Bs are very closely related, with HSPDEB3 being the most divergent form.
the three human PDE4 B isoforms are all expressed in COS 7 and U87 cells, and all three are expressed as soluble cytosolic and particulate associated forms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PDE4 family is the largest family of cAMP and cGMP specific phosphodiesterases and is the major source of cAMP hydrolytic activity in human brain.
we have cloned and characterized three human and rat cDNAs encoding novel splice variants of PDE4B, which are expressed in a variety of human tissues.
there are 4 human and 3 rat PDE4D splice variants that are different in their N terminal regions and that these differences are responsible for the differences in their properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PDE4B family of enzymes is more complex than we originally anticipated.
PDE4B3 is a novel splice variant of the PDE4B gene and that the PDE4 gene family has the potential to produce many more splice variants than have been identified so far.
the N terminal splice variants of HSPDEB1, HSPDEB2 and HSPDEB3 are different in catalytic activity, susceptibility to rolipram, and particulate association.
